19:46.sourceText: λέγων αὐτοῖς Γέγραπται Καὶ ἔσται ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς· ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ἐποιήσατε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
19:46.targetText: saying to them, “It has been written, My house is a house of prayer—but you made it a den of robbers.”

groups.note: Actual ἔσται is future indicative, while checked TR has present ἐστιν and English uses is. The shared being predicate is linked with the pinned future form explicitly preserved.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual Καί begins the written quotation in N1904. TR and English omit that additional opening and.

19:47.sourceText: Καὶ ἦν διδάσκων τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἀπολέσαι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ,
19:47.targetText: And He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy Him—also the chiefs of the people—

19:48.sourceText: καὶ οὐχ εὕρισκον τὸ τί ποιήσωσιν· ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἅπας ἐξεκρέμετο αὐτοῦ ἀκούων.
19:48.targetText: and they were not finding what they will do, for all the people were hanging on Him, hearing Him.

groups.note: Actual ποιήσωσιν is aorist subjunctive in the indirect what-to-do question. English uses they will do; no future-indicative source analysis is claimed.
Actual ἐξεκρέμετο is singular imperfect middle, agreeing with the singular collective people noun. English uses were hanging; the actual singular morphology and hanging/listening idiom are retained.

Actual genitive αὐτοῦ identifies the same person on whom the attentive hearing is directed. English states that person after hanging and repeats Him as the immediately coordinated hearing object; no second written accusative pronoun or different hearer/teacher is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual τό introduces the indirect what-to-do question; English renders that question without a separate nominalizing article.
